status: audition: nothing adopted; nobody has listened yet
purpose: Made-for-these-games sound effect candidates for the Magical Kingdom and Elevator Quest, three different ideas per slot, for the owner to choose by ear. Replaces nothing until picked.

tool.note: Audio can be fetched again from the flow with each candidate's sessionId and generationId.

price.observed: The first generation (K1-A, 0.5 s requested) was charged 2 credits at run time and priced 1.667 credits in its status. Every later price followed 3.333 credits per requested second (0.5 s 1.667, 0.7 s 2.333, 1.0 s 3.333, 1.5 s 5, 1.8 s 6, 2.5 s 8.333). The run-time charge is the price rounded to a whole credit. The estimate tool quoted 10 credits per second, about three times the price.

measurement.tool: ffmpeg decode to mono float, numpy; integrated loudness by ffmpeg ebur128 on the file padded with 1 s of silence

fields.activeS: from the first sample within 40 dB of the peak to the last within 50 dB of it
fields.attackMs: first sound to the peak sample
fields.riseTo6dbMs: first sound to the first sample within 6 dB of the peak
fields.first5msPeakDbfs: highest sample in the first 5 ms after the first sound
fields.last10msRelPeakDb: highest sample in the last 10 ms, relative to the peak

flagRules: sounding length (activeS) over the slot limit: 0.4 s for taps, ticks, the hop and the button; 1.2 s for chimes, the miss, the star and the cup; 1.5 s for arrival chimes and the hall bell; 2 s for flourishes and toys; 3 s for doors
hard start: riseTo6dbMs under 5 ms while first5msPeakDbfs is above -20 dBFS
measurement.listeningPages: Each candidate gain-adjusted only (no trim, fade or other change), so the three in a slot share one integrated loudness (listeningTargetLufs): -23 LUFS, or lower when a candidate would otherwise pass -1 dBTP after mp3 encoding. listeningPage.integratedLufs is the source loudness plus the gain; truePeakDbtp is measured on the page mp3. mp3 128 kbps. The five reference sounds are set to -23 LUFS (or their -1 dBTP limit) too, so they play louder on the page than in the game.
